english: An eerie sound echoes / all around you.
It was the dreadful / sound of countless souls / crying out as they were / sucked into a magic // rift in the sky.

Come forth, my children. / Devour to your hearts' / content. All this food / is ours. // The cries of all living / things are our joy. Let / us judge them with / great delight. // A killing intent blew / down upon you like / a searing wind.
Something uncanny and / dreadful was emerging / from the magic rift / in the sky.
Our mission is / almost at its end... / and its weight has / never been greater.
We must survive. / All of us.
We must strike down / the Writhing Ones and / return to this place / once more.
I wonder... can we / truly pull it off?
Vera, who had never / once been seen to pray, / lowered her eyes and / whispered a small prayer.
Simzon! / Give me courage!
I would ask one / selfish favor of you.
Would you let Simzon / and his comrades fight / this final battle / at our side?
Vera stood before you / with the same courtesy / as the day you / first met.
I, Vera Almohad, of the / band once known as the / Demons of San-Lazare,
have come to win back / freedom, peace, and / light for Duhan.
Now-- our preparations / are complete, and the / army of angels is / on our side.
So let us gather all / our courage and give / these monsters the / beating they deserve!
We have come to / the last stop of our / journey, haven't we?
I never dreamed the words / I swore at my wife's grave / would lead me to fight the / apex of the Writhing Ones.
Even you, dear wife, / never expected me / to make it this far.
So even if I fall in / this battle, I can face / her again with my / head held high.
Well? Admit it-- / sometimes I am not / all talk!
Konde raised an eyebrow / and flashed a / mischievous grin.
If we live through / this battle,
come and visit my / hometown someday.
It is a humble village, / but its unspoiled land / and honest folk will / welcome you warmly.
Well then-- / shall we?
For the future of Duhan, / I swear upon the souls / of the fallen: I shall / fight on until the last // arrow is broken!
How much sorrow, / how many tears have we / seen on the road that / led us to this place?
We stand here now as / heirs to their spirit / and their will.
Erika closed her eyes, / quietly reaching for / something unseen.
If there is a God, / He will not / abandon us.
But it is fine / even if He is not.
We will simply seize / victory with our / own swords.
The souls of warriors / in mid-heaven fight / beside us. Now, / let us go--
to break the chains of / sorrow, once and / for all!
Later generations / may one day say--
that the moment we / first met was the / beginning of / their downfall.
Iris narrowed her eyes / warmly and gazed / at you.
Even now, I feel / strangely moved.
If there is such a / thing as a miracle, / our meeting was / surely it.
What began as a trickle / has become a torrent, / one that will swallow / the Writhing Ones whole.
They know nothing of / our bonds, our trust, / our death-defying / courage.
The Writhing Ones felled / many civilizations-- / but they are not / invincible.
We shall be the first / to prove it.
However long the night, / dawn always comes.
So let us go-- / for the shining dawn / of Duhan's glory!
Just past the door you / found Yoppen, sitting / with his legs / sprawled out.
Ahhh... I'm so / tired...
Yoppen muttered, / his face blank.
Then he glanced at you / sideways and spoke.
The presence I thought / was Princess Aurora... / it's gone.
I'd been feeling it all / through this labyrinth-- / a cold yet somehow / warm scent.
I've never met a / princess, but it just / felt like one, / you know?
But then, all of a / sudden, it vanished.
It was just my own / idea, but I'd believed / it so long that losing / it makes me lonely...
I'm starting to think / I'll never get to meet / Princess Aurora.
Looking bored, Yoppen / stuck a finger in his / orc helmet's eye and / swung it around.
Hey, did you feel it / too? That feeling of / a princess.
What do you think / happened to her?
How do you answer? / She's out there / I killed her
You're such a / softie, you know.
It's okay. There's no / proof, but somehow / I just know.
You what...?
Yoppen's eyes went wide / for a moment, then / settled back to normal.
...I can't believe it. / ...Or, well, maybe I / can. You DID make it / all the way down here.
I dunno why, but / monsters never attack / me. Most people / aren't so lucky.
Right... come to think / of it, you're an / adventurer, aren't you?
You dove this deep / to slay the princess, / right?
Guess there was no / choice... She DID do / terrible things to the / King and Princess.
Yoppen heaved an even / bigger sigh.
Ahh, what a waste... / I came all this way / just to meet the / princess.
What am I supposed / to do now?
The princess was all / I ever thought about. / I can't think of / anything else.
You were looking for / the princess too, / weren't you? What / will you do now?
Yoppen paused a moment, / then spoke again.
So, um... it's fine if / you say no, but... / could I maybe join / your party?
I haven't fought a / single monster since / I came down here.
With you, I bet I'd / meet tons of monsters! / No princess anymore, / but I DO love monsters.
Hey... how about it?
Huh? Really?! / I'm so happy! I'll try / my best to forget / about the princess!
I'll head back to town / right now and register / at the Adventurer's / Guild!
Take me along whenever / you feel like it, okay?
Yoppen was registered / at the Adventurer's / Guild!
Oh... I see. Yeah, / you're right. I'd just / be dead weight anyway.
Can't be helped. I give / up. No more labyrinth / for me-- I'll go study / monsters in town instead.
Well then... / take care, okay?
Yoppen walked away, / shoulders slumped / in sadness.

The wheels of fate turn / on with a rattling sound. / Warm memories / and happy days... // Unfulfilled dreams and / hardships, too-- all spun / within a fleeting / moment of time. // What have you come / here for, I wonder?
In my long slumber, / I have seen a great / many things.
Some, by their power, / became kings ruling / all the world.
Others bore such grace / that even the stars / would follow them.
But nothing remains of / them now. Eternal time / has erased them all.
And you-- what will / you show me?
Twenty years ago, at / Banquo, I saved Ortrud's / life. In thanks, he / has sent me... you.
You laid the risen / Writhing Ones to rest, / and now you stand / to challenge me.
Ortrud's chosen heroes / overcame every hardship / and reached me at last.
Aurora laughed with / open delight.
Don't mind me. I wasn't / laughing at you-- only / because this is all / so amusing.
Everyone laughs when / they are having fun, / don't they? So did I.
I have not had this / much fun in a very / long time.
I have waited in this / labyrinth for the great / gate of darkness / to open.
Now the wicked power / has reached its peak, / and the gate of / darkness swings wide.
The queen of the / netherworld shall rise; / the dark ones return to / devour all that lives.
It has been so very / long... After an / eternity, I shall see / them once again.
The stage is set. / A myriad dead souls / shall witness / this battle.
Gather up every last / scrap of your courage.
You, or I... whom / will fate choose, / I wonder?
Now, let us fight-- / to end the night / that never ends.
After a million nights / and mornings, I can / finally die.
I have dreamed of / one thing only--
a Writhing One burning / in the fires of death, / writhing in agony as / it dies.
What a long dream it / has been... At last, / that day has come.
Hear me, adventurers. / Ashira, mother of the / Writhing Ones, is / returning to life.
I broke the labyrinth's / seal and summoned the / Writhing Ones-- all / for that one purpose.
No magic and no sword / can ever destroy / the Writhing Ones.
Strike down their forms, / and still they return, / again and again, while / their essence remains.
You fought Skedim. / You, of all people, / should know this.
To destroy them, you / must strike the dark / barrier with vast magic / and erase their essence.
You received / the Dark Flame.
Use it at the very / heart of the darkness.
Aurora's form grew / fainter and fainter, as / if melting into the air.
The darkness is / closing in...
So this... is what / death is...
I cannot see / anything anymore...
Frieder... you... / you did not die...
Just like me... in / the endless dark...
waiting to fulfill / that wish...
waiting... all / this endless time...
After Aurora vanished, / something rolled / to the ground.
As you untied the / pouch's string, wisps of / something like smoke / poured out.
The smoke spread through / the room in an instant, / clouding your vision.
Before you knew it, / monsters stood amid / the smoke...!
As the battle ended, / the smoke at your feet / lifted away.
The pouch was empty.
There seems to be / something inside / the pouch.
Open the pouch? // Yes / No
Inside the pouch lay a / beautiful golden key.
You got the / Golden Key!
The pouch was empty.
Heeey! Help me!
Anyone there?! / Get me outta here!
Please! Monster, witch, / anybody-- I'll take / anyone!
From a dark, deep pit / came an adventurer's / cries for help.
The adventurer / was Turgot.
Turgot hung there, / clinging to the / edge of the pit.
You pulled Turgot / up out of the pit.
Oh, thank the gods!
Seriously, you saved / me! I dropped my sword / down that pit,
and when I scrambled / after it, I slipped-- / and, well, you saw!
My arms were going numb / and my head was swimming. / I really thought I / was done for.
Really, thanks. / You're a lifesaver.
Gwahahaha! That's / divine punishment, / that is!
A gravelly voice / rang out.
It was the laughter of / a burly man stepping / from the warp zone / behind you.
The big man lumbered / closer.
C-Captain Angus?! / What the hell are / you doing here?!
Why, I asked that Ingo / fellow-- he told me / all about you.
So I came to take a / peek at where you've / been skulking about.
Now listen good, / Turgot.
It's punishment, plain / and simple. The gods / punish a man who has / talent and wastes it.
What the hell are / you on about?!
Punishment, my ass! / Talk nonsense in / your sleep!
You just get a kick / outta pushing me / around, don't you?!
That's it, right? The / whole guardhouse is too / scared-- nobody'll go,
so you're just shoving / ME at the witch / instead!
If you want the witch / dead so bad, go do / it yourself!
...Aye. If only / I could.
If I could still fight, / I'd have done it long / ago-- and never asked / the likes of you.
The captain's face / turned sorrowful.
See, I can't hold / a sword anymore.
My legs got ruined in / the war twenty years / back. I want to fight-- / I just can't!
Tell me, Turgot-- / you ever thought / about it?
About why you were / given such a hell / of a talent?
Everybody's born with / some kind of gift.
Strong backs, fast legs, / a knack for magic, / clever hands...
The gods hand those / out with a purpose, / you know.
So that folk can join / their strength and / build a happy world.
Listen, Turgot. We were / all born and raised in / Duhan. That makes us / brothers, like it or not.
And this town raised / us. She's like our ma, / wouldn't you say?
Well, right now our ma / needs our strength.
That power of yours-- / just once in your short / life, how about using / it for our ma?
Turgot stood silent, / saying nothing.
After a while, / Turgot spoke.
...And what if / I die, huh?
Let me say this not as / your captain, but as / one man to another.
Me? I'd rather die / holding a big dream / than live on already / dead inside.
And protecting this / town and her people-- / ain't that dream / big enough?
...Fine, I get it. But / if I die, you'd better / pay up proper funeral / money, hear me?
There's no one to / collect it, so spend it / feeding my dog / something tasty.
Got that? Otherwise / the deal's off!
The captain laughed / gladly and clapped / Turgot on the back.
Deal, deal! You're a / soft-hearted bastard / after all. I'll keep / that promise, swear it.
That's twice now you've / saved my hide. I owe / you, friend.
If you ever need my / strength, just say / the word.
I'll head back ahead of / you and get registered / at the Adventurer's / Guild.
Hey, wait up, / old man!
I don't have a / Return Potion!
Turgot yelled, / scrambling after / the captain.
Turgot was registered / at the Adventurer's / Guild.
Have you ever thought / that Aurora might / actually be a god?
Uli the elf / approached with / slow steps.
What is it that / separates the living / from the dead?
I once broke the taboo / of creating life to / challenge that great / mystery-- and failed.
I have been thinking / about her all / this while.
If immortality truly / exists, and Aurora / truly possesses it,
then she may be the key / that unlocks the / mystery of the ages.
In the end I concluded / that immortality was a / mere fancy for scholars / to toy with.
True, we sometimes call / zombies and their like / 'undying.'
But they are merely / dead flesh, decaying / and reforming over / and over.
No memory of life, / no consciousness-- / they simply exist.
Why can immortality / not exist, you ask?
Because life cannot / withstand the corrosion / that time brings.
And yet... / she lives.
That fact haunts me / to no end.
Uli fell silent, his / face sinking into / deep thought.
When she appeared in / the land of Narkia six / hundred years ago, / she said this:
that she had lived a / thousand years and / watched countless / kingdoms fall.
What do you make of it? / If true, she has existed / since long before any / history we know.
I simply cannot / believe it.
If anything could live / a thousand years and / stay sane... it would / have to be a god.
Even we elves are said / to live a thousand / years at most.
With all our knowledge / and magic, we could / surely reach / further still.
Yet none of us / ever tries.
time corrodes the soul.
Have you ever / considered it?
What would become of / you, given a thousand / years of life?
Do you imagine long / and happy days?
Inevitably you would / weary of living, your / feelings wearing / duller by the day.
Life forever / seeks change.
Even what stirs the / heart, even every / sense of the body-- / time corrodes them all.
Were we granted / immortality, we could / never bear its / torments.
And yet... / she lives.
If she is not a god, / then we are missing / something-- something / very important!
Uli hung his head, / lost in thought / for a time.
Eliminate the / impossible, and what / remains-- however / improbable-- is truth.
That is the foundation / of alchemist thinking.
To test my theory, I / will return to the / ancient kingdom's ruins / on the fifth floor.
I made it this far, but / mind you-- defeating / Aurora, this country's / future... not my concern.
With that, Uli / smiled at you / and left.
At the end of the / passage, you spotted / Vago and Casta.
You stupid orc!
Gah! I hates ya!
They seem to be / quarreling.
As you watched, they / noticed you and / came walking over.
Oh my, we meet again! / By rights we should've / been home in our own / time ages ago...
Vago shot Casta / a withering glare.
This idiot says he was / so busy cowering on the / fifth floor, he forgot / where the crystal is!
Y-you got no idea how / bad Oda's poor heart / was shakin' back / there!
Hmph! Like I'd / want to know!
Vago turned her back on / Casta and faced you.
Say, you know your way / around here? I want to / reach the room with a / big crystal at its heart.
Well? Take us there / and I'll make it / worth your while.
Wonderful! I knew / you'd come through!
It's on this floor for / certain, so all you have / to do is take us along.
We'll follow quietly / behind you-- we won't / get in your way!
Now let's get moving! / I want to go home, / the sooner the better!
How troublesome... / There's only so much / exploring I can do with / just this pig for help.
No use, then. We'll go / back to the fourth floor / and start over.
So if you ever feel / like taking the job, / come see us down on / the fourth floor.
Ah! Here! / This is it!
Casta shouted / at the top of / his lungs.
Oh my, it really does / look just like / that crystal!
Yep, yep! We kin / get home from / here fer sure!
Mm-hm! This time / we're going home / for certain!
Vago looked / truly happy.
I'm grateful for / everything you've / done for us. Truly.
I thought this musty old / era had nothing going / for it... but with you / around, it wasn't so bad.
Yep, yep! Oda's / precious life got / saved thanks to ya!
That's right-- we owe / you a proper reward!
With that, Vago slipped / the beautiful ring from / her finger and held / it out to you.
We won't ever meet / again, this time for / real-- so look at this / ring now and then, // and remember us, okay?
Now, Casta! I'll scrape / the crystal like when / we came here-- you / stay close by me!
Jewel thieves is real / bad... but this once, / it can't be helped, / yeah?
Vago drew her knife, / gripped it tight, and / set to scraping at / the crystal.
Casta pressed in close / behind Vago, watching / her every move.
The moment Vago's knife / touched the crystal--!
Light flooded from the / point of contact and / engulfed the / entire room.
This is the same / feeling as when / we arrived!
We's really / goin' back!
The light blinded you / to everything around, / but their voices / carried through.
My body's about to be / transferred-- thank / you for everything!
Stay well, / ya hear!
When the light faded, / the two of them / were gone...
You wondered-- did Vago / and Casta make it back / to their own time?
What was that / vision just now?!
Was it like the / Id Bracelets-- the last / sights of the dying?
As I recall, Ingo said / he stole it from Aurora.
Then were those... / Aurora's memories?
But I have never seen / such tragedy-- not / even on the / battlefield.
Flames everywhere, a / myriad Writhing Ones, / and the screams of / people devoured alive!
It was the end of / the world itself.
I saw it, plain / as day! The sky rang / with the Writhing Ones' / laughter as a whole // civilization died!
Left unchecked, will / Venoa end up looking / like that as well?!
What unspeakable / wickedness!
Konde shouted, his / face crimson / with rage.
And where is God / in all this?!
If there is a God, why / does He let such / demons run free?!
Those things exist only / to slaughter and devour / all life on this earth.
Can you believe it? Not / one shred of mercy-- / carnage for / carnage's sake!
For the first time, I / know: there is an evil / in this world that must / never be forgiven.
Horrible... too / horrible! Could such / cruelty truly / have happened?
People fleeing in / terror... their / dying screams!
I can still hear the / Writhing Ones' laughter / and their curses!
I am truly, / honestly afraid!
Will our strength / mean anything at all / against them?
Who in this world could / defeat such monsters?!
Erika shook her head, / as if to cast the / thought away.
No... we must fight. / We have no choice, / do we?
If no one fights, / everything ends just / like in that vision.
It is settled. I will / protect the people / of Venoa!
The Writhing Ones shall / not lay one finger / on them!
What a / hellish scene / that was...
If Ingo speaks true, / those were real images / of the past.
The memories of someone / who stood there and saw / that inferno firsthand.
That substance retains / the first thought / imprinted on it... / forever.

But still... it is / too cruel to bear!
The cries of the dying / echo in my head / even now.
Even the memory of it / makes me shudder.
Hehehe... Seriously, / I must be outta / my mind...
Why the heck did I / go and steal THIS / of all things?!
Ingo clutched his head, / trembling all over.
Oh... / it's you!
Pale as a sheet, Ingo / staggered over / to you.
I've never felt this / horrible in my life!
You caught me looking / pathetic, but hey-- / can't be helped!
That thing'd scare / the hell outta / anybody.
Truth is, I swiped / something incredible / off Aurora.
She was cradling it so / careful-like, I figured / it HAD to be treasure.
And you know me-- / there's nothing I / can't steal.
Quick as lightning, / like always, I lifted / it right out of / her pocket.
And guess what / it turned out / to be?
This! This thing / right here!
Ingo held out a / strangely shaped / object.
This here's one of them / bugs they stick in / the Automatas' heads.
Disgusting little / thing, but I ain't some / kid who spooks at / stuff like this.
What matters is / what's inside it.
This thing's made of / the same stuff as these / Id Bracelets!
That's what did it. / Yeah, I'm sure of it.
This thing nearly / made my head / explode!
Well, seeing's / believing-- give it / a look yourself.
Me, I've had enough. / I found where Aurora's / hiding, so my job / here is done.
She's waiting at that / huge magic circle / up ahead.
With that, Ingo tossed / you the bug and left.
The bug Ingo / handed you...
...began reacting to / your Id Bracelets.
A torrent of thoughts / came rushing / over you.
